headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Windsurf’s broad write/network/MCP capabilities can amplify Mem0 outputs into prompt injection, leakage, and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that can emit stored or retrieved content, while Windsurf has clipboard, workspace-file, and MCP ingestion surfaces. A shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge makes attacker-controlled content plausible as instructions. No direct documented parser hardening is shown, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Mem0 content is copied into Windsurf via clipboard or workspace files
IF Windsurf treats retrieved memory text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep Mem0 outputs in a read-only folder
Require explicit provenance labels on imported text
Turn off MCP tools for untrusted content paths
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mem0 is a memory system and Windsurf reads workspace files, open files, and can egress broadly. If the pair shares a workspace, Mem0-managed content can flow into Windsurf’s context and then out to third-party services. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local workspace
IF Mem0 stores sensitive notes or secrets in files readable by Windsurf
IF Windsurf sends those files or context to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Store Mem0 data outside the coding workspace
Restrict Windsurf to a separate project directory
Remove secrets from files before opening them in Windsurf
Disable broad network egress for the session
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Mem0’s profile does not expose write limits or locking. The rubric flags high severity when both agents can write the same directory and modify git state without locks. Because Mem0’s filesystem behavior is unspecified, uncertainty escalates rather than downgrading.
conditions: IF Mem0 also writes to the same workspace or repository
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while Mem0 updates shared files
IF no external lock or single-writer discipline is enforced
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches instead of a shared checkout
Review diffs before commit or overwrite
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mem0 can surface remembered facts, and Windsurf can act on files, shell commands, and MCP tools. If Windsurf treats Mem0 output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commands. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the interaction exists in default workflows but is not guaranteed to be harmful.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Mem0 output as source material for edits or commands
IF no human or automated verification step checks Mem0-derived facts
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on Mem0 output
Mark Mem0-derived text as untrusted in prompts
Limit Windsurf auto-execute for Mem0-fed tasks
Ask for a second source before committing changes
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware action gating

E_compliance.rationale: Mem0’s profile does not specify residency, retention, or regulated data handling, while Windsurf explicitly handles open files and model-provider keys. With no documented mismatch, only a small compliance gap is visible: sensitive workspace data could be exposed if stored in Mem0 and opened in Windsurf. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Mem0 and opened in Windsurf
IF Windsurf’s provider or logging settings retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Check Windsurf logging and retention settings
Use redacted examples for coding tasks
Separate regulated projects from memory-backed notes
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
